_comment: Curated exact-ID -> canonical parameter-size TOKEN pins (GH#9). TOP precedence tier: an entry here overrides the mechanical ExtractParamSizeToken decomposition AND the fetch-owned ParamSizeFor fallback (pin > mechanical > ParamSizeFor), so a curated identity size can never be flipped by an ollama-bot refresh or a greedy scan. KEYING: 'id' is the lowercase exact model ID (matched case-insensitively). VALUE: 'param_size' is the canonical size token verbatim (e.g. '17b-16e', '10.7b'); an EMPTY param_size is a SUPPRESS-pin — NO size is extracted for that ID (no #size segment, no shape ints) — used for size-shaped tokens that are not sizes. Presence, not the value, decides: a suppress-pin's '' never falls through to the mechanical extractor. CURRENT ENTRIES: (1) every catalog llama-4 scout/maverick ID that LACKS the expert-count suffix is pinned to its full-shape token ('17b-16e' for scout / '17b-128e' for maverick) so every variant of the artifact keys to ONE entity. That set was censused over the vendored catalog with BOTH legs: every ID whose decomposition yields family llama + version 4 + variant scout|maverick, UNION a literal ID sweep for the 'llama4'/'llama-4' substrings. The 4 dotted Bedrock forms (meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0, us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0, meta.llama4-scout-17b-instruct-v1:0, us.meta.llama4-scout-17b-instruct-v1:0) escape a substring-only census and are therefore enumerated explicitly below; each mechanically extracts only '17b', so its pin is load-bearing. (2) upstage/solar-10_7b-instruct -> '10.7b' (underscore-glued decimal; '_' is not a separator so the mechanical extractor cannot reach it). (3) qwen/qwen3-coder-next-fp8-1m -> '' (suppress: '1m' is a 1M-context tier marker, not params). New entries are appended as curation identifies further under-specified spellings or size-shaped tokens that are not sizes.
